```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7)
```

BlackThriveSS makes a fixed set of public dashboard evidence available in R: a
catalogue of force, council and national datasets from 2018 onwards, the
dashboard's force ranking chart for any year and group, and links that carry a
chart to and from the dashboard website. The package includes all the data used
in this tutorial; running it needs no network connection or dashboard session.

## Install and discover

Before CRAN publication, use the supplied installation bundle or a source
archive and its required dependencies. The package itself is pure R. Source
installation of some dependencies can require a compiler; on Windows and macOS,
use available CRAN dependency binaries. Installation instructions accompany the
release; `install.packages("BlackThriveSS")` is not yet a supported public route.

```{r discover}
library(BlackThriveSS)
btg_datasets()
btg_releases()
```

## Load the evidence

```{r load}
x <- btg_get_data()
x
head(x$data[c("force", "ratio", "months_supplied", "coverage_status")])
```

The object contains ordinary data frames in `x$data` and `x$coverage`, plus
explicit `metadata` and `selection` lists. This snapshot has 44 force rows,
including British Transport Police, and 528 monthly coverage entries. The
dashboard display rule allows 40 force ratios. An eligible ratio does not imply
that a force supplied all 12 months.

The fixed release identifies the July 2026 source archive used by the local
dashboard, whose aggregates were built in September 2026. It is not a statement
about the newest data available online. Specify a release when writing a
reproducible analysis:

```{r pinned}
release <- btg_releases()$release[1]
met <- btg_get_data(force = "metropolitan", years = 2025, release = release)
met$data[c("black_stops", "white_stops", "black_population", "white_population", "ratio")]
```

## Browse the catalogue

`force_disparity` is the package's original dataset. The catalogue release
adds every year the dashboard holds and all four groups compared with White,
plus national and council tables. Each dataset is read with the same function
and verified against its checksum:

```{r catalogue}
y <- btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year", groups = "Black", years = 2022:2025)
y
head(y$data[c("force_label", "year", "group", "ratio", "rank", "coverage_status")])
btg_get_data("national_year")$data[c("year", "stops", "arrest_rate", "hit_rate")]
```

The 2025 Black rows of `force_ethnicity_year` reproduce `force_disparity`
exactly. Coverage differs by year: the dashboard verifies monthly submissions
only inside a recent window, so earlier years are `unverified`, which is not
the same as missing. The final source year is incomplete, and
`months_in_source` says how many of its months the source month covers.

```{r council}
lambeth <- btg_get_data("council_ethnicity_year", council = "E09000022", years = 2025)
lambeth$data[c("group", "group_stops", "white_stops", "ratio")]
```

Council counts depend on stop coordinates, which some forces do not publish,
so they undercount and carry no display rule or rank.

## Recreate and edit the chart

```{r chart, fig.alt="Ten highest displayed Black to White stop-rate ratios in 2025, with asterisks for partial reporting."}
p <- btg_plot_disparity(x)
p
```

The bars reproduce the dashboard ranking's values and ordering. This static
ggplot uses portable system fonts; it does not include interactive hover text
or previous-year change annotations. An asterisk and a lighter fill mark
partial or unverified reporting, and each bar carries its 95% interval. Counts
are not annualised.

Any year and group in `force_ethnicity_year` can be drawn, and one force can
be highlighted as the dashboard's selected force:

```{r chart-year, fig.alt="Asian to White stop-rate ratios in 2024 with the Metropolitan Police highlighted."}
btg_plot_disparity(btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year"), year = 2024, group = "Asian",
                   highlight = "metropolitan")
```

Use `ranking = "lowest"` or `ranking = "closest"` to change the ordering and `n`
to choose the maximum number of bars. Force subsets retain ranks from the full
release. The returned plot can be styled with ordinary ggplot2 functions:

```{r customise, eval=FALSE}
p + ggplot2::labs(title = "My local evidence briefing")
ggplot2::ggsave("disparity.png", p, width = 11.5, height = 7.5, dpi = 160)
```

```{r figure-data}
head(btg_figure_data(p)[c("force_label", "ratio", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "coverage_status")])
```

The figure table describes the original evidence. User-added ggplot layers or
styles do not alter that table or the saved evidence specification. For your own
calculations, transform a copy of `x$data`; the reproduction functions reject
modified evidence or provenance.

## Check reporting coverage and consistency

```{r coverage}
btg_coverage(met)
checks <- btg_validate(x)
checks[c("check", "passed")]
stopifnot(all(checks$passed))
```

`btg_validate()` verifies release integrity and internal consistency, including
monthly-to-annual totals, ethnicity subtotals and calculated rates. It does not
certify that all events were recorded. A missing submission remains `NA`, not
zero. For example, this snapshot has no 2025 returns for Greater Manchester or
Gwent; their annual counts remain missing.

```{r missing}
btg_get_data(force = c("greater-manchester", "gwent"))$data[
  c("force_label", "total_records", "months_missing", "coverage_status")]
```

## Save an exact evidence view

```{r replay}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
btg_save_view(p, path)
recreated <- btg_from_view(path)
stopifnot(identical(btg_figure_data(p), btg_figure_data(recreated)))
unlink(path)
```

Use a durable file path in your own project when you want to keep the view.
The JSON pins the release, payload checksums, selected forces and chart version.
The original bundled example is also installed with the package. Unknown
releases or incompatible versions fail rather than substituting newer data.
Custom ggplot styling is not saved. Pixel identity requires matching fonts and
graphics dependencies; the evidence table is the reproducibility contract.

## Round-trip with the dashboard website

The dashboard describes every view in its address. `btg_dashboard_url()` turns
a chart into the link that opens the Disparity page at the same year, group and
selected force, and `btg_from_url()` reproduces the chart behind a link copied
from the website's Share view button:

```{r links}
chart <- btg_plot_disparity(btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year"), year = 2024,
                            group = "Asian", highlight = "metropolitan")
link <- btg_dashboard_url(chart)
link
back <- btg_from_url(link)
stopifnot(identical(btg_figure_data(back), btg_figure_data(chart)))
```

The default link form is read by every deployed dashboard version, but it
carries only the year, group, display and selected force. The `format =
"state"` form also carries the ranking order and the source month, so a chart
ordered by closeness to parity survives the trip only in that form:

```{r links-state}
closest <- btg_plot_disparity(btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year"), year = 2024,
                              group = "Asian", ranking = "closest")
stopifnot(identical(btg_figure_data(btg_from_url(btg_dashboard_url(closest, format = "state"))),
                    btg_figure_data(closest)))
```

`btg_from_url()` warns when a link was made from a different source month than
the snapshot. A link selects a view; the website recomputes its numbers from
its current release, while the chart in R stays pinned to the snapshot. Set
`options(BlackThriveSS.dashboard_url = ...)` to link to another deployment.

## Cite and interpret responsibly

```{r cite}
btg_citation(x)
citation("BlackThriveSS")
```

The data dictionary is installed at:

```{r dictionary}
system.file("NOTES", "data-dictionary.md", package = "BlackThriveSS")
```

Rates divide recorded group events by Census 2021 residents. These denominators
are not measured 2025 street exposure. The counts are events, not unique people;
the aggregate cannot separate vehicle-only searches. Police officer-defined
ethnicity differs from Census self-reported ethnicity. Approximate Poisson
intervals condition on observed counts and fixed populations, and do not capture
missing returns, repeat stops or classification uncertainty. A ratio is not an
individual stop probability or a causal estimate of discrimination.

## Common problems

* **Package not found:** install the release first, and add its chosen library
  with `.libPaths(c("/path/to/library", .libPaths()))` in a fresh session.
* **Unknown force:** use the exact identifiers in `btg_get_data()$data$force`.
* **Unsupported year:** `force_disparity` holds 2025 only; use
  `force_ethnicity_year` for other years, within the range `btg_datasets()` shows.
* **Link cannot be reproduced:** only Disparity page links are supported, and
  the expanded Black definition rests on self-defined ethnicity the package does
  not bundle.
* **No eligible ratios:** BTP, City of London or a missing-return selection may
  have no displayable resident-based comparison; inspect counts and coverage.
* **Changed evidence:** obtain a fresh object with `btg_get_data()`. Keep custom
  analysis in a separate data frame.
* **Unknown release or checksum mismatch:** obtain the package release that
  carries that snapshot. Editing a view identifier would change the evidence.
